3:00|
4:19|Return NotImplemented, not False, upon rich comparison with unknown type
5:46|Comparison methods should ideally return ``NotImplemented`` when unable to make sense of the arguments. This way, the comparison is delegated to the reflected method on the other object, which might support the comparison (see https://docs.python.org/3/reference/datamodel.html#object.__lt__, and your own article on the subject, https://github.com/sympy/sympy/blob/master/doc/src/python-comparisons.rst).

9:60|class Foo():

If ``sympy.Basic.__eq__`` instead returned ``NotImplemented``, the statement ``s == f`` would delegate to ``Foo.__eq__``, thus maintaining a symmetric relation.
